# Wave 3 transcript hardening: final independent review

## Verdict: PASS

**Exact reviewed and executed source commit:** `d3edcf859f7067da67520f42d9efb6e64d155f94`.

The transcript hardening fix passes this independent review. All previously identified false-acceptance bypasses reject, including all six class/module lifecycle and cleanup skips preceded by diagnostic stdout without a trailing newline. All five original successful logs remain accepted, totaling 651 distinct test records.

This verdict applies to the transcript parser and the reviewed regressions at this commit. It supersedes the changes-required verdicts for the earlier parser commits. It does not claim that full CI, the complete phase 4 gate, or unrelated changes in the combined commit were independently verified by this reviewer.

## Source review

The final parser change removes the line-start anchor from the lifecycle expression and uses `lifecycle.search(line)`, allowing a negative lifecycle record to be detected after diagnostic output on the same line. The required unique announcement count, pending result state, summary count, plain final `OK`, unsuccessful result handling, and error-header rejection remain unchanged.

The added regression executes real unittest class and module setup, teardown, and cleanup functions that print without a newline and then raise `SkipTest`. It asserts that all six transcripts reject after changing only the terminal summary to plain `OK`.

## Independently reproduced results

I reran the same 48-case independent probe used for the preceding review, changing only its source commit and output artifact paths. It extracts the parser AST from the exact Git object, so later working-tree modifications cannot affect the executed implementation.

| Probe group | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Original four class setup/teardown error and skip bypasses | All rejected |
| Class setup, teardown, cleanup skips after stdout without newline | All three rejected |
| Module setup, teardown, cleanup skips after stdout without newline | All three rejected |
| Other negative cases: ordinary failure, failing subtest, method skip, expected failure, unexpected success, lifecycle errors/skips, loader error | All rejected |
| Successful docstring and split stdout cases | Both accepted |
| Quiet successful class/module setup, teardown, cleanup | All six accepted |

**48 generated cases:** all 34 negative cases rejected; eight success cases accepted; six known successful lifecycle stdout cases remain falsely rejected as documented below. There were **zero incorrect acceptances** in this probe. This is not a claim that all 48 cases matched their ideal acceptance expectation.

### Original logs

| Original log | Accepted records |
|---|---:|
| baseline.log | 175 |
| build.log | 225 |
| evidence.log | 36 |
| harness.log | 99 |
| submodules.log | 116 |
| **Total** | **651** |

Logs were read from `/workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/p004-artifacts/p004-source-00b172d8b1363c2f21deb3cbd0fb29a908ea86fc`.

## Remaining limits

The parser still rejects six genuinely successful class/module setup, teardown, and cleanup probes when diagnostic stdout without a newline prefixes the next test announcement. This was reproduced on the preceding commit and remains unchanged. It fails closed, does not affect the 651 original records, and is outside the false-acceptance fix being approved. Supporting that additional output shape would require a separate framing improvement.

A text parser cannot authenticate an entirely fabricated but internally consistent transcript. Artifact provenance and source binding remain separate responsibilities. This probe is bounded to the available Python runtime and ordinary unittest output, and does not establish compatibility with arbitrary custom runners or all possible diagnostic text.

I did not independently rerun the root's reported 72 targeted tests or 184 baseline tests. Those reported totals are not included in this review's independently verified results.

## Reproduction

```sh
python3 -B /workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/w3_transcript_accepted_probe.py
```

The script obtains the exact function from:

```sh
git show d3edcf859f7067da67520f42d9efb6e64d155f94:tools/compat/logic-pro/run_baseline.py
```

The source and test diff were independently inspected with:

```sh
git show d3edcf859f7067da67520f42d9efb6e64d155f94 -- tools/compat/logic-pro/run_baseline.py tests/compat/logic-pro/baseline/test_baseline_gate.py
```

Evidence files:

- `/workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/w3_transcript_accepted_probe.py`
- `/workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/w3_transcript_accepted_probe.json`
- `/workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/w3_transcript_accepted_probe.log`

The script's exit status reports completion of the investigation; the JSON's `accepted` and `expected_accept` fields distinguish expected behavior from the six documented conservative rejections.

## Provenance

This review uses repository code, independently constructed genuine unittest executions, and the supplied original logs. No external implementation or restricted material informed it. No repository files were edited and no Git state was changed.
